items.title: 1.8 Reactions of Na and Mg with water, oxygen and chlorine

source_refs.note: Topic 1.8, printed page 15: the heading topic whose detail is in 1.8.1 to 1.8.3; the period 3 original is placed here.

blocks.text: Sodium, in group 1, and magnesium, in group 2, both react with water, oxygen and chlorine, but sodium is the more reactive metal in each case. Their reactions, taken one by one in the next three topics, illustrate the trend in metallic character across period 3: sodium, with one valence electron, a larger atom and a lower ionization energy, loses its electron more readily than magnesium.

blocks.alt: A chart of the period 3 elements sodium to chlorine. An orange band lists their oxides with oxidation numbers and marks them basic, amphoteric or acidic; a blue band lists their chlorides, neutral or acidic in water. Below, two boxes: the equations of sodium and magnesium with water, oxygen and chlorine, and the acid-base equations of the oxides and chlorides.
blocks.caption: Period 3 oxides and chlorides, and the reactions of sodium and magnesium (original chart after Table 1.2 and the equations of topics 1.8 to 1.10).
blocks.long_description: Sodium reacts vigorously with water to give sodium hydroxide and hydrogen, magnesium slowly, though with steam it gives magnesium oxide; both burn in oxygen, sodium with a golden flame to the peroxide and magnesium with an intense white flame to the oxide; both give white chlorides with chlorine. Along the period the oxides pass from basic ionic lattices (sodium, magnesium) through amphoteric aluminium oxide to acidic covalent molecules (silicon to sulfur), the chlorides from neutral ionic salts to covalent compounds that hydrolyse to acidic solutions, and the oxidation numbers rise from +1 to +6 with the group's valence electrons.

blocks.prompt: Before reading the three reactions, predict which of sodium and magnesium reacts faster with cold water and why.
blocks.explanation: Sodium: it is larger than magnesium, has a lower first ionization energy and only one electron to lose, so it is the more metallic and the more reactive, and it reacts vigorously while magnesium reacts slowly.

items: Sodium and magnesium both react with water, oxygen and chlorine; sodium is the more reactive because of its greater metallic character.
